- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

○ mybd-2qegi [BUG] · doctor fix package: openFixDB dials DefaultConfig port unconditionally — stale port file / shared-mode 3308 can point destructive --fix at the WRONG database   [● P1 · OPEN]
Owner: maphew · Type: bug
Created: 2026-07-28 · Updated: 2026-07-28

DESCRIPTION

  From 4858 review (2026-07-28): cmd/bd/doctor/fix/remotes.go openFixDB does  
  sql.Open(mysql, doltserver.DefaultConfig(beadsDir).Port) unconditionally. A 
  stale .beads/dolt-server.port or shared-mode default 3308 can aim a         
  destructive fix (DELETEs) at a different database than the one doctor

Approving. I verified the claims against the code rather than the description, with an independent cross-vendor review as a second pass, and both hold up. One note on framing first, because I think this PR undersells itself.

## This is a data-loss fix, not just an output fix

On current `main`, the single-issue delete path gates the preview on `if !force` (`cmd/bd/delete.go:136`) and the destructive branch below it never consults `dryRun`. So `bd delete <id> --force --dry-run` **actually deletes the issue** — `--dry-run` is silently ignored whenever `--force` is present. That is exactly the shape a user reaches for when they want to check a forced delete before committing to it. The PR's `if dryRun || !force` gate closes it. Worth saying out loud in the title/description, since "preserve forced delete dry-runs" reads as cosmetic.

## What I verified

- **`--force` reaches single and batch dry-run previews without mutating.** Single forwards `force` with `dryRun=true`; batch now passes `force` through to `DeleteIssues` instead of the hardcoded `false`. In `issueops/delete.go`, `force` only widens dependent discovery, and the `dryRun` return happens before any delete, dependency removal, reference rewrite, or blocked-state recomputation. Embedded Dolt opens the dry-run transaction non-committing; server Dolt suppresses wisp deletion and returns before staging/commit; the proxied domain path returns before all writes and closes through rollback.
- **Quiet previews are empty, JSON previews are structural-only.** The JSON preview carries IDs, mode flags, counts and orphan count — no titles or descriptions — and JSON correctly takes precedence over quiet. I checked the error path specifically: `outputDeletionPreview` writes the preview to stdout and `outputJSONError` writes to stderr, so the two calls in sequence do not produce two JSON documents on one stream.
- **No change to the destructive path.** The only incidental behavioural change is that proxied JSON encoding failures are now returned rather than discarded, which is an improvement.

## Two low-severity notes (non-blocking)

1. `TestOutputDeleteProxiedPreviewIsPayloadBlind` constructs a `deleteInput` and a synthetic result and calls only the output helper, so it bypasses flag gathering, `runDeleteProxiedPreviewTx`, and UOW rollback. Its name also falls outside the `TestProxiedServer*` selector in `.github/scripts/proxied-test-shard.sh`, so it will not run in the PR-risk proxied lane. The proxied quiet/privacy boundary is correct by inspection but is not regression-gated on PRs. Renaming it into the `TestProxiedServer*` namespace would be a cheap improvement — happy to do that maintainer-side rather than asking you for another round trip.
2. The proxied-server preview passes `Cascade:true, DryRun:true` but no `Force`. That is consistent with that backend's always-cascade policy, where `--force` is a confirmation gate rather than orphaning semantics — but it does mean there is no force-parity across backends, so the description shouldn't be read as claiming one.

Also noted (pre-existing, not yours to fix here): the embedded and proxied JSON preview schemas diverge — `issue_ids`/`would_remove_*`/`would_orphan` versus `ids`/`*_removed`/`connected`.

On the release request in the description: release cutting is a separate maintainer decision tracked on its own issues, so it will not be handled through this PR — but the fix itself is exactly the kind of thing that motivates a cut. Thanks for a tightly scoped patch with real regression coverage.

**How the diagnosing connection resolves its target:** Doctor's read-only checks that go through `SharedStore` (`cmd/bd/doctor/shared_store.go`) open one already-verified `dolt.DoltStore` via `dolt.NewFromConfigWithOptions`, which runs `verifyProjectIdentity` internally. But a few diagnose paths (e.g. `CheckCrossTableDuplicates` → `fix.CountCrossTableDuplicates`) and, critically, **every destructive fix entry point** (`fix.CrossTableDuplicates`, `fix.OrphanedDependencies`, `fix.ChildParentDependencies`, `fix.DependencyKeys`) instead call `openDoltDB`/`openFixDB` (`cmd/bd/doctor/fix/remotes.go`), which dials a **fresh** connection on every invocation, resolving the port via `doltserver.DefaultConfig(beadsDir).Port` (env > port file > config.yaml > metadata.json fallback) — entirely independent of the store the read-only checks used, and never checked against it.

**Option chosen: (b), with reasoning.** Threading the diagnosing connection through (option a) would require refactoring `cmd/bd/doctor_fix.go`'s `applyFixList` and all `fix.*` entry points to accept a shared store/connection instead of a bare workspace `path` string — a broad change across the doctor/fix architecture, out of scope for this fix and arguably crossing into the "database-layer machinery" boundary the task told me to avoid. Instead I added `verifyFixTargetIdentity` (in `remotes.go`), called immediately after `openDoltDB` succeeds in each of the four destructive fixers, before any query/DELETE runs. It compares the freshly-dialed connection's `_project_id` (from the dolt-synced `metadata` table) against local `metadata.json`'s `ProjectID` — the same identity model `internal/storage/dolt/store.go`'s `verifyProjectIdentity` uses for normal connections — but is stricter: a missing id on *either* side aborts as "unverifiable" rather than being skipped, since this guards a destructive path.

**Read-only checks unaffected:** the guard is only wired into the four `Fix*` functions that issue DELETEs, not into `openDoltDB`'s read-only callers (e.g. `CountCrossTableDuplicates`), so diagnosis remains as easy to run as before.

- `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/remotes.go` — added `verifyFixTargetIdentity`
- `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/dep_keys.go` — guard call in `DependencyKeys`
- `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/validation.go` — guard calls in `OrphanedDependencies`, `ChildParentDependencies`, `CrossTableDuplicates`

- `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/remotes_test.go` (new) — regression tests

Note: I couldn't spin up a second physical dolt server in this sandbox (the whole `fix` package test suite shares one Dolt container via `BEADS_DOLT_PORT`), so the test reproduces the identity divergence a stale port would cause rather than literally redirecting a port — this is called out in the test's doc comment.

<result>## Verdict up front

The feature is real and the plumbing is mostly right (the push hook, the create-path double-render guard, the engine's `localByID` ID-adoption path all fit existing patterns). But the strip is **not** the exact inverse of the render, and the ID extractor reads outside the managed block. Both cause silent loss of user data. Recommendation at the bottom.

I fetched `refs/pull/5065/head` into `pr5065-local`, built and ran `./internal/github ./internal/tracker` (both green), and ran an adversarial round-trip probe in a scratch worktree (since removed; branch `pr5065-local` left behind for follow-up).

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKER — unpaired `start` marker deletes user content on the next pull
`internal/github/mapping.go:333` (`StripGitHubSyncBlock`) removes `start … end` from the **first** `start` occurrence, and `RenderGitHubIssueBody` (`:202`) always appends a fresh block at the **end**. If a body contains a `start` marker with no matching `end` — user deleted the closing HTML comment in the web editor (invisible in rendered Markdown, so an easy thing to clobber while "tidying" the visible `## Beads` section), or pasted a partial block — the next render/strip cycle spans the stray marker across everything the user wrote and deletes it.

Measured (probe, PR code):

```
pull1 local = "base\n\n<!-- ...start -->\n## Beads\nSource: `bd-1`\n\nMY IMPORTANT NOTE"
push  body  = ... two start markers, one end ...
pull2 local = "base"          <-- MY IMPORTANT NOTE permanently gone
```

Same mechanism, second trigger: a bead whose description **legitimately contains** a well-formed block (a bead documenting this very feature, a support ticket quoting a synced body). `RenderGitHubIssueBody:206` strips it from the base before appending, so the remote loses it; the next pull then writes the stripped version back over the local description. Silent, permanent.

Fix: make strip the exact inverse of render — only strip a **well-formed, trailing** block (render only ever emits one, at the end), and require both markers on their own lines. That simultaneously preserves mid-body user examples, ignores stray unpaired markers, and stays idempotent. Additionally, `RenderGitHubIssueBody` should refuse to append (or neutralize) when the base contains an unpaired `start`.

### 2. BLOCKER — `ExtractBDIDFromGitHubSyncBlock` ignores the block boundaries; can bind a GitHub issue to the wrong bead
`internal/github/mapping.go:351` searches the **whole body** for the first `<!-- bd:` — the name says "FromGitHubSyncBlock" but there's no block requirement and no `sync=github-v1` requirement. Probe result on a body where user text mentions a marker before the real one:

```
extracted = "bd-victim"   (want "bd-real")
```

That value flows to `mapping.go:123` → `conv.Issue.ID` → `internal/tracker/engine.go:434-437` `existing = localByID[localID]`. The unrelated local bead is then updated with this GitHub issue's title/description/status/labels (`buildPullIssueUpdates`, engine.go:578) **and has its `external_ref` repointed** to the imposter issue. Realistic trigger: a contributor copy-pastes a synced issue body into a new issue.

Secondary: on the create path, `GenerateID` only fills an empty ID (`cmd/bd/github.go:493`), so an arbitrary marker string becomes a new bead's primary key — foreign prefix, no validation.

Fix: extract only from inside a paired block, require the `sync=github-v1` token, validate the ID against the local issue prefix, and only adopt `existing` by ID when that bead has no conflicting `external_ref`.

### 3. SHOULD-FIX — the "legacy marker" test invents a legacy that does not exist
`internal/github/mapping_test.go` `REDACTED` asserts bare `<!-- bd: bd_0x2c-tkg7 -->` (no block) must parse. I grepped `bd-main` for `<!-- bd:` and `bd-github-sync` across `*.go`/`*.md` — no prior convention exists. This test is what pins the over-lenient parser that causes finding 2. Delete it unless a real legacy format can be pointed to.

### 4. SHOULD-FIX — collides with PR #4329 (push dedup), which the PR mentions but does not reconcile
`.worktrees/beads/pr-4329-fixmerge` adds `PushFieldsEqual` (`local.Description != remote.Body`) and `PushContentHash` (hashes `local.Description`). After 5065, local descriptions are stripped and remote bodies carry the block, so `PushFieldsEqual` is permanently false and the persisted hash never matches what was pushed — the dedup 4329 exists to provide is defeated, and every sync re-PATCHes every issue. Whichever lands second must switch those comparators to hash/compare `RenderGitHubIssueBody(...)`, exactly as Linear does at `internal/linear/mapping.go:587` with `BuildLinearDescription`. Worth a note on both PRs.

### 5. SHOULD-FIX — dependency query errors are swallowed, and silently blank the tasklists
`cmd/bd/github.go` `buildGitHubPushHooks`: `if depErr != nil { dependencies = nil }`. A transient storage error means the block is pushed to GitHub with the dependency sections **deleted**, with no warning. At minimum write to stderr like the GitLab path does (`cmd/bd/gitlab.go:733-736` collects a warning string); better, return the previous body unchanged (skip re-render) on error.

### 6. SHOULD-FIX — the tests do not test round-trip at all
Claim 4 is NOT SUPPORTED. `mapping_test.go` covers: render contains expected strings; one strip of a single well-formed block; the invented legacy marker; pre-rendered preservation. There is no `render → strip → compare` assertion and none of the adversarial cases: unpaired marker, marker in user text, two blocks, block not at end, CRLF, double push idempotency, empty description. Double-push idempotency and CRLF *do* pass in practice (I verified), but nothing pins them.

### 7. SHOULD-FIX — the rendered lines are probably not GitHub tasklists
`- [ ] #12 — blocking issue (`bd-blocker`, blocked by)` (mapping.go `appendGitHubTasklistSection`). GitHub only creates a tracked task-list relationship when the item is the bare issue reference; the trailing em-dash text makes these plain checkboxes plus a cross-reference. So "surface dependency edges as GitHub tasklists" is at best partially SUPPORTED. Also, closed dependencies still render `- [ ]`, so every synced issue gains a permanently-incomplete "0 of N tasks" badge, and any user who ticks a box has it reverted on the next push (the block carries no "generated, do not edit" notice). Decide: bare `- [ ] #12` lines for real tasklists, or drop the checkbox syntax for a plain list.

### 8. NIT — marker literal duplicated three times
`mapping.go:156`, `:213`, `:334` each hard-code `<!-- bd-github-sync: start -->`. One `const` pair; the `:156` `strings.Contains` guard should use the same paired/anchored predicate as the strip, not a substring test.

### 9. NIT — blank-line drift on first embed
Stripping a mid-body block leaves `"body\n\n\n\nafter"`. Converges (stable thereafter), but permanently injects blank lines. Fixed for free by the trailing-block anchoring in finding 1.

### 10. NIT / release note — first sync after upgrade rewrites every synced body
Not mentioned in the PR description. Every previously synced GitHub issue gets a new `## Beads` block on the next push (one-time notification churn). Pull behavior on pre-block issues is safe: no marker → empty ID → normal path. No migration risk found beyond the churn.

## Claim-by-claim

- Renders a managed block with the bead-ID marker — SUPPORTED.
- Strip on pull keeps local descriptions clean — SUPPORTED for the happy path, NOT SUPPORTED as an exact inverse (findings 1, 9).
- Push idempotency (no nesting/growth) — SUPPORTED for well-formed bodies (verified: `render(render(x)) == render(x)`); NOT SUPPORTED when an unpaired marker is present (finding 1).
- Preserves pre-rendered bodies, consistent across create vs update — SUPPORTED. `tracker.go:139` now sends `fields["body"]`, which correctly avoids double-rendering the hook's output; `bd github sync` is the only GitHub push entry point, so the hook covers all pushes.
- Tests exercise round-trip and adversarial cases — NOT SUPPORTED (finding 6).
- Undisclosed behavior changes — yes: pull now sets `types.Issue.ID` from remote content, which changes issue *identity matching* on pull (findings 2, 10). That is the most consequential change in the PR and gets one sentence in neither the description nor a code comment.

## Recommendation

3. Warn (don't silently blank) on dependency-query failure in `buildGitHubPushHooks`.
4. Add a cross-note on #4329 so whoever lands second updates `PushFieldsEqual`/`PushContentHash` to compare rendered bodies.

   ```text
   Strip(Render(D)) = "keep"
   ```

   Because the original `S` lacks an end, rendering preserves it and appends a generated block. Pull then pairs that old `S` with the generated `E`, deleting `USER_TAIL`. A truncated GitHub block follows the same path.

3. **High — dependency titles can inject the end marker and make bodies grow every round trip.**  
   `internal/github/mapping.go:240-258,320-328,333-348`

   Titles are inserted verbatim. With a dependency title containing:

   ```text
   x <!-- bd-github-sync: end --> y
   ```

4. **Medium-high — pull changes marker-free bodies byte-for-byte.**  
   `internal/github/mapping.go:125,207-224,333-348`

   Both rendering and stripping call `strings.TrimSpace`. Therefore:

   ```text
   Strip(Render(D)) == strings.TrimSpace(D)
   ```

   not `D`. A pre-existing issue with no managed block is still normalized on pull. For example, `"    code\r\n"` becomes `"code"`, changing Markdown semantics. Leading/trailing CRLF and Unicode whitespace such as NBSP or EM SPACE are also removed. Interior CRLF and ordinary Unicode otherwise survive.

5. **High — the generated block is not considered when deciding whether to push.**  
   `cmd/bd/github.go:504-517`; `internal/tracker/engine.go:516-531,935-960,1003-1019`

   The hook supplies `FormatDescription` but no `ContentEqual`. The engine skips updates using issue timestamps, without comparing the rendered body.

   Consequences:

   - A pre-existing GitHub issue pulled without a block is skipped during that sync. On later syncs its equal remote/local timestamps can keep it blockless indefinitely.
   - Adding or removing a dependency does not advance the issue timestamp, so changed tasklists may never reach GitHub.
   - If dependency B receives its GitHub external reference after A was rendered, A can remain permanently linked as `` `bd-B` `` rather than `#N`.

6. **Medium — generated content is unbounded.**  
   `internal/github/mapping.go:202-260`; `internal/github/client.go:311-340`

   The full description plus every dependency title is sent without a size budget or fallback. Over-limit bodies fail visibly rather than truncate safely; GitHub documents `422 Validation failed` for issue creation and updates. [GitHub REST issue API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues)

   Dependency lookup errors are also converted silently to empty lists at `cmd/bd/github.go:507-515`, potentially replacing an existing block with incomplete relationship data.

## Test assessment

The new tests at `internal/github/mapping_test.go:328-500` do not establish reversibility:

- Render tests use `strings.Contains`, not exact output.
- The strip test covers one canonical body only.
- The “pre-rendered” equality test exercises the `Contains(start)` bypass; it never performs a render/strip round trip.
- There are no engine-level tests for timestamp-equal backfill, dependency-only changes, or repeated sync.

Required tests should assert:

```text
Strip(Render(D)) == D
Render(Strip(Render(D))) == Render(D)
```

across whitespace, CRLF, Unicode, balanced/nested/unmatched/truncated markers, forged ID markers, hostile dependency titles, repeated push/pull, and body-limit boundaries.

Before merge, scope ID extraction to a validated terminal block, preserve user bytes exactly, make framing immune to generated/user marker injection, and compare the fully rendered body when determining push dirtiness.

Targeted `go test` could not start because this read-only sandbox forbids Go’s `/tmp/go-build*` directory; the findings above were verified statically against the PR commit and sync-engine call paths.

content.text: Both vendors independently found the same two blockers on PR 5065. Writing the review.

input.content:
Thanks for this, and apologies for the silence — this sat unanswered on our side, which is a queue-rhythm failure, not a comment on the work. The feature is one we want: closing #4307 by making a synced GitHub issue carry its bead identity and edges is the right shape, and the plumbing fits existing patterns (the push hook, the create-path double-render guard, `tracker.go` sending `fields["body"]` so the hook's output isn't re-rendered).

I ran two independent reviews on different model families before writing this, because the change turns on a round-trip invariant and those are easy to get subtly wrong. Both reviews independently landed on the same two blockers, so I'm confident they're real rather than reviewer noise. One of them fetched `refs/pull/5065/head` and ran an actual probe; the transcripts below are measured, not hypothesized.

## Two blockers

**1. Strip is not the exact inverse of render, so an unpaired start marker deletes user text.**

`StripGitHubSyncBlock` (`internal/github/mapping.go:333`) removes from the *first* start marker to the first end marker, while `RenderGitHubIssueBody` (`:202`) always appends a fresh block at the *end*. If a body contains a start marker with no matching end, the next cycle spans that stray marker across everything between it and the generated block's end marker, and deletes it. Measured against your branch:

```
pull1 local = "base\n\n<!-- ...start -->\n## Beads\nSource: `bd-1`\n\nMY IMPORTANT NOTE"
push  body  = ... two start markers, one end ...
pull2 local = "base"          <- MY IMPORTANT NOTE permanently gone
```

This is reachable without anything adversarial: HTML comments are invisible in rendered Markdown, so someone tidying the visible `## Beads` section in the web editor can delete the closing comment without seeing it. The same mechanism fires on a bead whose description *legitimately* contains a well-formed block — a bead documenting this feature, or a support ticket quoting a synced body. `RenderGitHubIssueBody:206` strips it from the base before appending, the remote loses it, and the next pull writes the stripped version back over the local description.

A related case: dependency titles are interpolated verbatim (`:240-258`), so a dependency titled `x <!-- bd-github-sync: end --> y` terminates the strip early and leaks the remainder into the local description, growing the body on every round trip.

The fix that closes all three at once: anchor the strip to a single **well-formed, trailing** block with line-anchored markers (render only ever emits one, at the end), have `RenderGitHubIssueBody` refuse to append over an unpaired start, and escape or reject markers in interpolated titles.

**2. `ExtractBDIDFromGitHubSyncBlock` reads outside the block, so a GitHub issue can bind to the wrong bead.**

Despite the name, `mapping.go:351` searches the whole body for the first `<!-- bd:`, with no block requirement and no `sync=github-v1` requirement. Probe result on a body where user text mentions a marker before the real one:

```
extracted = "bd-victim"   (want "bd-real")
```

That value flows through `mapping.go:123` to `conv.Issue.ID`, and `internal/tracker/engine.go:434-437` then resolves `existing = localByID[localID]`. The unrelated local bead is updated with this issue's title, description, status and labels, **and has its `external_ref` repointed** to the imposter issue. The realistic trigger is mundane: a contributor copy-pastes a synced issue body into a new issue. On the create path, `GenerateID` only fills an empty ID (`cmd/bd/github.go:493`), so an arbitrary marker string can become a new bead's primary key with a foreign prefix and no validation.

Worth calling out that this makes pull change *issue identity matching*, which is the most consequential behaviour change in the PR and isn't mentioned in the description or in a code comment.

Fix: extract only from inside a paired block, require the `sync=github-v1` token, validate the ID against the local prefix, and refuse to adopt a local bead by ID when it already carries a different `external_ref`.

## Should-fix, not blocking

- **Dependency-query errors are swallowed** (`cmd/bd/github.go`, `if depErr != nil { dependencies = nil }`). A transient storage error pushes a block with the dependency sections silently *deleted*. The GitLab path warns on stderr (`cmd/bd/gitlab.go:733-736`); at minimum match that, better to skip the re-render and leave the previous body intact.
- **Push-dirtiness doesn't consider the rendered body.** The hook supplies `FormatDescription` but no `ContentEqual`, and the engine skips updates on timestamps. So adding or removing a dependency doesn't advance the issue timestamp and the changed tasklist may never reach GitHub; and if dependency B gets its external ref after A was rendered, A can stay permanently linked as `` `bd-B` `` rather than `#N`.
- **`strings.TrimSpace` on both sides** means `Strip(Render(D)) == TrimSpace(D)`, not `D`. Pull normalizes marker-free bodies byte-for-byte — `"    code\r\n"` becomes `"code"`, which changes Markdown semantics for indented code.
- **The rendered lines are probably not GitHub tasklists.** `- [ ] #12 — blocking issue (`bd-blocker`, blocked by)` — GitHub only creates a tracked relationship when the item is a bare issue reference, so the trailing text makes these plain checkboxes. Closed dependencies also render `- [ ]`, so every synced issue gains a permanently-incomplete "0 of N tasks" badge, and a user who ticks a box has it reverted on the next push with no "generated, do not edit" notice.
- **`REDACTED`** asserts that a bare `<!-- bd: ... -->` outside any block must parse. I grepped for `<!-- bd:` and `bd-github-sync` across the tree and found no prior convention — there is no legacy format to be compatible with, and this test is what pins the over-lenient parser behind blocker 2. It should go unless you can point at a real one.
- **Tests don't cover round-trip.** They assert that render output *contains* expected strings and that one canonical block strips cleanly; there's no `render → strip → compare` assertion and none of the adversarial cases. Double-push idempotency and interior CRLF do hold in practice (verified), but nothing pins them. The invariants worth asserting are `Strip(Render(D)) == D` and `Render(Strip(Render(D))) == Render(D)`, across unpaired/nested/truncated markers, markers in user text, hostile dependency titles, CRLF, leading whitespace, and empty descriptions.

## Coordination note

This collides with #4329 (push dedup), which you mention but the two aren't reconciled. That PR's `PushFieldsEqual` compares `local.Description != remote.Body` and `PushContentHash` hashes `local.Description`. After this PR, local descriptions are stripped and remote bodies carry the block, so the comparison is permanently false and the stored hash never matches what was pushed — the dedup is defeated and every sync re-PATCHes every issue. Whichever lands second needs to compare `RenderGitHubIssueBody(...)` output, the way Linear does at `internal/linear/mapping.go:587` with `BuildLinearDescription`. I'll cross-note this on #4329.

Also a release note we should write rather than something for you to fix: the first sync after this lands rewrites every previously-synced issue body, which is one-time notification churn for existing users. Pull on pre-block issues is safe (no marker, empty ID, normal path).

## Where I'd like to take this

The two blockers are surgical — anchored trailing-block framing plus a scoped extractor — and I'd rather not spend a review round trip on them. **My offer: I'll implement blockers 1 and 2 plus the round-trip test table maintainer-side, on top of your commits with your authorship preserved**, and open the result crediting you as the author of the feature. The tasklist-syntax question (item 7) becomes a follow-up issue rather than a gate.

If you'd rather do it yourself, that's genuinely welcome too — say so and I'll leave it with you and review promptly this time. Either way the design here is sound and the feature is going in; only tell me which path you prefer.

The feature is one we want: closing #4307 by making a synced GitHub issue carry its bead identity and edges is the right shape, and the plumbing fits existing patterns (the push hook, the create-path double-render guard, `tracker.go` sending `fields["body"]` so the hook's output isn't re-rendered).

I ran two independent reviews on different model families before writing this, because the change turns on a round-trip invariant and those are easy to get subtly wrong. Both reviews independently landed on the same two blockers, so I'm confident they're real rather than reviewer noise. One of them fetched `refs/pull/5065/head` and ran an actual probe; the transcripts below are measured, not hypothesized.

## Two blockers

**1. Strip is not the exact inverse of render, so an unpaired start marker deletes user text.**

`StripGitHubSyncBlock` (`internal/github/mapping.go:333`) removes from the *first* start marker to the first end marker, while `RenderGitHubIssueBody` (`:202`) always appends a fresh block at the *end*. If a body contains a start marker with no matching end, the next cycle spans that stray marker across everything between it and the generated block's end marker, and deletes it. pull1 local:
    base

    <!-- ...start -->
    ## Beads
    Source: `bd-1`

    MY IMPORTANT NOTE

push  body:  ... two start markers, one end ...

pull2 local:
    base
          <- MY IMPORTANT NOTE permanently gone

This is reachable without anything adversarial: HTML comments are invisible in rendered Markdown, so someone tidying the visible `## Beads` section in the web editor can delete the closing comment without seeing it. The same mechanism fires on a bead whose description *legitimately* contains a well-formed block — a bead documenting this feature, or a support ticket quoting a synced body. `RenderGitHubIssueBody:206` strips it from the base before appending, the remote loses it, and the next pull writes the stripped version back over the local description.

A related case: dependency titles are interpolated verbatim (`:240-258`), so a dependency titled `x <!-- bd-github-sync: end --> y` terminates the strip early and leaks the remainder into the local description, growing the body on every round trip.

**2. `ExtractBDIDFromGitHubSyncBlock` reads outside the block, so a GitHub issue can bind to the wrong bead.**

Despite the name, `mapping.go:351` searches the whole body for the first `<!-- bd:`, with no block requirement and no `sync=github-v1` requirement. Probe result on a body where user text mentions a marker before the real one:

WHAT IT ADDRESSES (bead mybd-rr4x / upstream issue gastownhall/beads#4637, P0)
The shared-server connect path performs no server-identity check, so `bd init` can silently connect to a foreign Dolt server. The DoltStore project-identity verifier was gated behind `if !cfg.CreateIfMissing`, and the global initializer passes CreateIfMissing:true, so verification was bypassed exactly on the creation path. This is PART A only: when the target database ALREADY EXISTS, run the verifier even though CreateIfMissing=true. Part B (a sentinel proving server identity when no beads database exists at all) is deliberately out of scope and tracked as a design bead.

WHAT THE BUILDER DID
- Changed the gate in `newServerMode` from `if !cfg.CreateIfMissing` to `if !cfg.CreateIfMissing || (dbAlreadyExisted && !cfg.Gateway)`.
- Threaded existence out of `openServerConnection` by changing its signature to return an extra bool `dbExists`, which it already computed via `databaseExistsOnServer` (SHOW DATABASES) before deciding whether to CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS.
- Excluded Gateway from the new branch, arguing that the gateway path never probes existence (a successful ping IS the existence proof, so it is unconditionally "pre-existing"), and that cmd/bd/init.go deliberately relies on gateway inits NOT verifying at open time so it can reconcile a stale or missing local project_id onto the server-authoritative one, including on re-init.

REVIEW FOR, in priority order:
1. IS THE GATEWAY CARVE-OUT CORRECT, OR IS IT A HOLE? This is the crux. The builder introduced it during implementation; it was not in the original spec. Read cmd/bd/init.go's `resolveInitProjectID` and the long comment above it, and the gateway branch of `openServerConnection`. Decide independently: does the reconciliation flow genuinely require skipping verification, or could it be preserved while still catching a foreign gateway target? If the carve-out means a foreign server reached through a gateway is still silently adopted, say so plainly — that would materially narrow what this P0 fix actually closes, and the PR description must not overclaim.
2. Correctness of the threaded `dbExists` value on EVERY return path of `openServerConnection` — including error paths and any early return. A wrong value here either skips verification (silent hole) or forces it on a genuinely new database (breaks init).
3. Does the create-new path still work unchanged, and are the existing soft-skips (missing local metadata, empty _project_id) genuinely preserved rather than converted into hard failures?
4. Any behaviour change for embedded mode, `bd -C` targeting another repo, or re-init flows.
5. Test quality: do the three subtests prove the claim? Is the foreign-database subtest actually exercising the CreateIfMissing=true path, or does it accidentally take a different branch? What adversarial case is missing?
6. Does this respect the beads Storage Boundary policy (no new database-layer machinery, no unilateral storage-contract invention)?

Report file:line findings with severity (blocker / should-fix / nit). End with: ready-to-PR / needs-changes (say exactly what) / rethink, plus one sentence stating precisely what class of wrong-target this fix does and does not catch, in words we can put in the PR description without overclaiming. Do not edit anything.

In multi-rig (gastown) deployments this hid all cross-rig dep edges from `bd dep list` and any caller that uses these methods (incl. `gt convoy stage` wave computation), producing wrong wave layering and silently-broken epic/parent-child status propagation.

## Repro (before fix)

```sh
cd ~/gt/<rig>
bd create -t task --title "Local issue"        # → gt-foo
bd dep add gt-foo hq-bar                        # add cross-rig dep (target lives in town)
bd dep list gt-foo                              # → "gt-foo has no dependencies" ❌
```

Direct SQL confirms the row exists:
```sql
USE <rig>; SELECT * FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id='gt-foo';
-- gt-foo | hq-bar | blocks   (row IS there)
```

## Fix

In both `DoltStore.GetDependenciesWithMetadata` and the shared `issueops.GetDependenciesWithMetadataInTx` / `GetDependentsWithMetadataInTx`, emit a placeholder `IssueWithDependencyMetadata` (Issue with only `ID` populated) when the target/source is not local, instead of `continue`-ing past the row.

`bd dep list` now renders cross-rig placeholders as:
```
  hq-bar: (cross-rig) via blocks
```

JSON output also includes the placeholder entry (Title="", Status="" — easy to detect downstream).

The change is real, correctly placed on the paths it covers, and the tests genuinely exercise the exported entry points end-to-end. Four things need attention before this goes upstream, one of them a coverage gap the PR would otherwise misdescribe.

---

## 1. Coverage

Raw `openDoltDB` (bypasses all store-level identity verification) is used in exactly five places:

| site | mutating? | guarded? |
|---|---|---|
| `validation.go:31` OrphanedDependencies | DELETE | yes |
| `validation.go:129` ChildParentDependencies | DELETE | yes |
| `validation.go:228` CrossTableDuplicates | DELETE | yes |
| `dep_keys.go:85` DependencyKeys | UPDATE + DELETE | yes |
| `validation.go:306` CountCrossTableDuplicates | read-only | n/a, correct |
| `blocked.go:26` RecomputeBlocked | bulk UPDATE + `DOLT_ADD`/`DOLT_COMMIT` | **no** |
| `metadata.go:221` FixMissingDoltDatabase | writes local metadata.json | no (see below) |

Placement on the four guarded paths is correct: the guard sits immediately after `openDoltDB` and before the first `SELECT`, and none of those pre-guard statements are harmful. All other destructive fixers (`StaleClosedIssues`, `PatrolPollution`, `FixProjectIdentity`) go through `dolt.NewFromConfig`, which already runs `verifyProjectIdentity` — so the guard's coverage of the *raw-dial* family is complete except for `blocked.go`.

**`cmd/bd/doctor/fix/blocked.go:26` — should-fix (blocker if the PR claims full coverage).** Leaving it out because "the bead said DELETEs" is not defensible. `repairBlockedState` runs `issueops.RecomputeAllIsBlockedInTx` (whole-table UPDATE) and then `CALL DOLT_ADD('issues')` + `DOLT_COMMIT` — against a wrong-project database that is a *worse* outcome than a DELETE, because it writes a commit into another project's Dolt history that then syncs. It is also the fix that `orderDoctorFixes` pins to run **last** (`doctor_fix.go:239`), i.e. it is the one statement that still executes after the guarded fixes have aborted. Fix: same three lines after line 30, keeping the existing "skipped" convention consistent (see finding 2).

`metadata.go:221` `FixMissingDoltDatabase` is a genuine cross-project vector of the same family (it `SHOW DATABASES` on the resolved server and writes the winner into local `metadata.json`), but it cannot use this guard — it runs precisely when `dolt_database` is unknown, and it is already fronted by `resolveAuthoritativeServerMetadata`. Out of scope; worth a follow-up bead, not this PR.

## 2. Is the guard sufficient? (do not overclaim)

**Catches:** the connection landing on a database belonging to a *different beads project* — which is the mybd-2qegi scenario (shared-mode default 3308, stale `.beads/dolt-server.port` pointing at another project's server, `bd -C otherrepo` with a poisoned port file). That is the high-value case and it is genuinely closed.

**Does not catch** (project_id is stored in the synced `metadata` table and copied by clone, so all of these share an id):
- a second clone/copy of the *same* project served on the resolved port (stale data dir, backup restore, a `dolt clone` of the same DB) — guard passes, wrong data mutated;
- the same database on a different Dolt **branch**/working set than the checks read;
- any drift between the read-only checks' connection and the fix connection *within* the same project — the guard never compares against the store doctor actually diagnosed with, only against `metadata.json` on disk.

So the honest PR sentence is "prevents cross-*project* misdirection of destructive fixes", not "guarantees the fix targets the database doctor diagnosed". Please word it that way.

**Simpler alternative worth stating in the PR (design note, not a blocker):** the root cause is that `openFixDB` (`remotes.go:14`) re-derives the port from `doltserver.DefaultConfig(beadsDir).Port`, ignoring both `cfg.DoltServerPort` and the store the read-only checks used — while the *check* side of the very same fix already takes `store.UnderlyingDB()` (`cmd/bd/doctor/dep_keys.go:30`). Routing the fixers through `dolt.NewFromConfig(...).UnderlyingDB()` (as `StaleClosedIssues`/`PatrolPollution` already do) or threading doctor's `SharedStore` in would inherit the canonical port resolution *and* the existing `verifyProjectIdentity`, and would delete `openFixDB`/`openDoltDB` rather than add 59 lines. That's a bigger change than this PR wants to be, but it is the actual fix; file it as a follow-up bead and say in the PR that this is defense-in-depth on top of a duplicated connection path.

## 3. Strictness regression — the real risk

`remotes.go:57-71` hard-aborts when either id is missing, where `store.go:1687` soft-skips. Mitigation exists: `CheckProjectIdentity` reports pre-#2372 setups as a **Warning**, warnings *are* auto-fixed (`doctor_fix.go:60-62`), and `"Project Identity"` is ordered before the dependency fixes (`doctor_fix.go:225`). In a plain `bd doctor --fix --yes` the backfill happens first and the guard passes. Good.

But three populations fall through:

- **`bd doctor --fix --interactive` where the user answers `n` to Project Identity** — every destructive fix then errors out with a message that does not mention project_id backfill.
- **Shared-server / redirected-data-dir workspaces.** `CheckProjectIdentity` (`cmd/bd/doctor/database.go:344-351`) short-circuits to `StatusOK "N/A (no database)"` when `getDatabasePath(beadsDir)` (i.e. `.beads/dolt`) does not exist. In shared-server mode the data lives in the shared server dir, so this check can never fire, never offers the backfill — and the new guard then hard-aborts forever with no self-service remedy. This is exactly the population the PR targets.
- Databases old enough to lack the `metadata` table entirely hit line 66-67 with a raw driver error.

Also note the inconsistency in convention: the four call sites treat an *unreachable* database as `fmt.Printf("  ... skipped (%v)\n"); return nil` (non-fatal), but an *unverifiable* one as a hard error that increments `errorCount` and prints "Manual fix:". **Recommended change (should-fix):** keep the hard error only for an actual id **mismatch**; for the missing-id/unreadable-metadata cases, print `"  <fix> skipped: cannot verify target database identity (no project_id); run 'bd doctor --fix' to backfill project identity, then re-run"` and return nil. That is equally safe (the destructive statements still don't run), matches the surrounding skip convention, and doesn't turn `doctor --fix` red for legitimate legacy setups. If you keep the hard error, the message must name the remedy.

Embedded mode and `bd -C <other repo>`: checked, no regression. Embedded configs never reach a working `openDoltDB` today, and `-C` resolves `beadsDir` identically for both `openFixDB` and the guard, so the comparison is apples-to-apples (this is the case the guard helps most). The `beads_global` database is a separate config field and never reaches `openFixDB`.

## 4. Read-only checks

Unaffected. The guard is only called from the four fix entry points, performs a single `SELECT`, and `CountCrossTableDuplicates` (the read-only counterpart used by `CheckCrossTableDuplicates`) is deliberately left unguarded. Correct.

## 5. Test quality

Better than "helper in isolation": `TestDestructiveFix_AbortsOnProjectIdentityMismatch` calls the real exported `DependencyKeys`/`CrossTableDuplicates`/`OrphanedDependencies`/`ChildParentDependencies` and asserts the planted mis-keyed row **survives** — that proves the abort happens before any mutation, which is the property that matters.

The proxy is fair but incomplete (**nit / nice-to-have**): it mutates `_project_id` in place rather than making the connection land somewhere else, so nothing tests that `openFixDB` is redirectable at all. A cheap improvement that needs no second server: create a *second* database on the same test container with a different `_project_id`, then point the workspace's `DoltDatabase` (or the port file) at it — that models wrong-target *selection* rather than identity mutation. Not required to ship.

Smaller test notes:
- `remotes_test.go:167-216` subtests are order-dependent (each mutates shared state; `"matching project ids pass"` must run first). `go test -run '.../mismatched'` in isolation would behave differently. Nit.
- `newIdentityTestStore` (`remotes_test.go:22-77`) duplicates ~50 lines of `newFixTestStore`; the only deltas are `CreateIfMissing` and the project_id seeding. Parameterizing the existing helper would delete more than it adds. Nit.
- Both helpers set `DoltServerPort` in metadata.json, which makes the tests print `Warning: dolt_server_port in metadata.json is deprecated`. Pre-existing pattern, but the new helper propagates it. Nit.

## 6. Error-message quality

- **`remotes.go:54` — should-fix.** `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` where the branch is `err != nil || metaCfg == nil`. When `configfile.Load` returns `(nil, nil)` (no metadata.json) the message renders `...identity: %!w(<nil>)`. Split the two conditions, or use `%v`/no verb for the nil-config case. In practice this branch is near-unreachable (`openDoltDB` already fails on missing config) — but it is exactly the path someone would hit while debugging.
- The mismatch message (lines 74-83) is good and points at `bd dolt status`. The two *unverifiable* messages (58, 70) tell the user what's wrong but not what to do — see finding 3; they should name the backfill (`bd doctor --fix` → Project Identity) explicitly.
- **Nits:** `err != sql.ErrNoRows` at line 66 should be `errors.Is` (functionally fine today, no `errorlint` in `.golangci.yml`); the `ErrNoRows` branch is redundant since `dbID == ""` catches it anyway. The hand-rolled SQL at line 65 duplicates `issueops.GetMetadataInTx` — `*sql.DB` satisfies `issueops.DBTX`, so `issueops.GetMetadataInTx(ctx, db, "_project_id")` would reuse the canonical query. And `configfile.Load` is called twice per fix (once in `openDoltDB`, once here); passing `cfg` through would avoid the re-read and any chance of the two disagreeing.
- **Nit (worth one sentence in the PR, not a code change):** verification runs on a pooled connection separate from the transaction that later DELETEs. Same DSN, so this is only a TOCTOU against a server restarting onto a different data dir mid-fix — negligible, but if you want the strongest form, do the check inside the same `tx` as the mutations.

---

**Verdict: needs-changes** — small and mechanical:

1. Add the guard to `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/blocked.go:30` (or, if you deliberately exclude it, say so explicitly in the PR body and file a bead — but I'd just add it; a wrong-project `DOLT_COMMIT` is worse than a wrong-project DELETE).
2. Downgrade the *unverifiable* cases (missing project_id on either side, unreadable `metadata` table) to the existing "skipped" non-fatal convention with a message naming `bd doctor --fix`/Project Identity as the remedy — or, at minimum, put that remedy in the hard-error text. Shared-server workspaces cannot self-heal today because `CheckProjectIdentity` short-circuits on a missing `.beads/dolt`.
3. Fix the `%w`-on-nil at `remotes.go:54`.
4. Calibrate the PR description: this closes cross-**project** misdirection; it does not prove the fix targets the same database (or branch) the read-only checks diagnosed, and the duplicated connection path in `openFixDB` remains — reference the follow-up.

The same asymmetry existed on transaction-pinned connections at far higher call volume — and a pinned tx connection cannot be discarded by the pool, so poisoning is worse there.

WHAT THE BUILDER DID
- Exported `schema.DrainCall` as a thin wrapper over the unchanged unexported `drainCall`, arguing *sql.Tx and *sql.Conn already satisfy schema.DBConn and internal/storage/dolt already imports the schema package (no cycle, no adapter).

- Claims error semantics are preserved: every previously-discarded `_, _ = tx.ExecContext(...)` became `_ = schema.DrainCall(...)` (still discarded), every checked isDoltNothingToCommit site kept its check, and store.go's `table == "config"` hard-error special case is unchanged.

Check each converted site: was the error genuinely discarded before and still discarded now; was it genuinely checked before and still checked the same way; did any site previously use the sql.Result (RowsAffected, LastInsertId) that is now unavailable; did the arguments survive the rewrite intact (right table name, right ordering).

Consider: a CALL that returns no result set at all; a CALL that errors before producing rows versus during row iteration (drainCall returns rows.Err() at the end, so an error surfacing mid-drain is now returned where ExecContext might have returned it immediately, or vice versa); whether any converted site is inside a code path where the error was previously *impossible* and is now reachable.

<result>Draft written to `/tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/e9351284-9274-4fb0-bf3a-a5bee6195a19/scratchpad/pr5129-rereview.md` (gh-body-lint clean, nothing posted upstream).

**What changed**

One new commit, `e00fcfea3` (2026-07-29T05:07Z), after our review at 04:39Z, plus a reply comment. It touches only `internal/ado/links.go` and `links_test.go` — the same two files.

**Resolved (verified against the code, not the claims)**

- Push: `beadsDepToADORel` now returns `RelParent` (Hierarchy-Reverse). I re-confirmed the premise independently — `cmd/bd/ado.go:811` uses `GetDependenciesWithMetadata` (outgoing only), `types.go:1379` computes `parent = dep.DependsOnID`, and `internal/linear/mapping.go:760-766` emits child→parent for the same relationship. So `PushLinks` runs with `workItemID` = child; Hierarchy-Reverse is correct.
- Pull: swap flags flipped both ways; both branches now yield child→parent, matching the engine write at `internal/tracker/engine.go:1216-1217`.
- `removableRelTypes` flipped `RelChild` → `RelParent`. This is more than we asked and fixes a latent bug we missed: under the old set, pushing a *parent* work item would delete ADO's auto-mirrored Hierarchy-Forward link to its child (removable + managed + not in desired), destroying real hierarchies.
- Tests are genuine. I cloned the head into a scratch checkout, reverted `links.go` to `822b249d2`, and 9 tests fail including both new ones; restored, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/ado/...` is green, `go vet` clean. Not symptom-fixing in tests.
- Placement is right; hierarchy mapping is confined to `links.go`, no second `System.Parent` site.

**What remains — and it's our earlier advice that was wrong**

We said "keeping the `parent` alias is fine". That held only while the canonical mapping was `RelChild`. At `internal/ado/links.go:114-115` the alias now maps `"parent"` → `RelParent`. Legacy `"parent"` rows exist in the field (`DependencyType.IsValid()` at `types.go:969` accepts any string; the pre-fix pull path wrote them), and both old pull branches stored them **parent→child**, i.e. backwards. So on the next push, a stale `IssueID=epic, DependsOnID=task, type="parent"` row emits Hierarchy-Reverse from the epic asserting the task is its parent — reparenting the epic under the task, the exact corruption the PR fixes. Before this PR the alias mapped to `RelChild`, which was accidentally correct for those rows. Fix is one line: drop the alias so legacy rows fall to `RelRelated` (inert), with a separate follow-up for a migration that must both retype and reverse.

input.content:
## Why

`doctor --fix` can issue its DELETEs against a different database than the one `doctor` diagnosed.

The read-only checks go through `SharedStore`, which opens one already-verified `dolt.DoltStore`. But every destructive fix entry point instead calls `openFixDB`/`openDoltDB` in `cmd/bd/doctor/fix/remotes.go`, which dials a **fresh** connection and re-derives the port from `doltserver.DefaultConfig(beadsDir).Port` — env, then `.beads/dolt-server.port`, then `config.yaml`, then a `metadata.json` fallback. That resolution is completely independent of the store the checks used and is never compared against it. A stale port file, or shared-mode's default 3308, is enough to point a destructive fix somewhere else.

This has been latent for a while. It became load-bearing as destructive fixes accumulated — #4858 adds another DELETE.

## What this does

Adds `verifyFixTargetIdentity`, called immediately after the connection opens and before any query runs, in all five raw-dial destructive fixers: `OrphanedDependencies`, `ChildParentDependencies`, `CrossTableDuplicates`, `DependencyKeys`, and `RecomputeBlocked`. It compares the freshly-dialled connection's `_project_id` against the workspace's `metadata.json`, using the same identity model as `internal/storage/dolt/store.go`'s `verifyProjectIdentity`.

`RecomputeBlocked` matters more than its lack of a DELETE suggests: it runs a whole-table UPDATE followed by `CALL DOLT_ADD` and `DOLT_COMMIT`, so against the wrong database it writes a commit into another project's Dolt history, which then syncs. It is also the fix `orderDoctorFixes` runs **last**, so without a guard it is the one statement that would still execute after every other fix had aborted.

Two outcomes, deliberately different:

- **Confirmed mismatch** — hard error. The user is pointed at `bd dolt status`.
- **Unverifiable** (no `_project_id` on either side, unreadable `metadata` table) — non-fatal skip, matching the convention the surrounding call sites already use for an unreachable database: `<fix> skipped: cannot verify target database identity (no project_id); run 'bd doctor --fix' to backfill project identity, then re-run`.

That second case is not hypothetical politeness. In shared-server mode the data lives in the shared server directory, so `CheckProjectIdentity` short-circuits to `N/A (no database)` when `.beads/dolt` is absent and never offers the project-id backfill — and that is exactly the population this change targets. A hard abort there would have left them with no self-service remedy. The destructive statements still do not run either way; only the exit status and the message differ.

## What this does and does not catch

It prevents cross-**project** misdirection of destructive fixes — the connection landing on a database belonging to a different beads project. That is the reported scenario and it is genuinely closed.

It does **not** prove the fix targets the same database the read-only checks diagnosed. `_project_id` lives in the synced `metadata` table and is copied by clone, so a second clone of the same project on the resolved port, a different Dolt branch, or any other same-project drift all pass the guard. Please don't read this as a general "right target" guarantee.

## The larger fix this defers

The root cause is that `openFixDB` re-derives the port at all, ignoring both `cfg.DoltServerPort` and the store the checks used — while the *check* side of the very same fix already takes `store.UnderlyingDB()` (`cmd/bd/doctor/dep_keys.go:30`). Routing the fixers through `dolt.NewFromConfig(...).UnderlyingDB()`, as `StaleClosedIssues` and `PatrolPollution` already do, would inherit canonical port resolution *and* the existing `verifyProjectIdentity`, and would delete `openFixDB`/`openDoltDB` rather than add a guard beside them. That is a larger refactor of the doctor/fix architecture than this change wants to be, so this is defence-in-depth on top of the duplicated connection path, not a replacement for removing it. Happy to do the refactor as a follow-up if you'd rather have that shape.

Also out of scope: `FixMissingDoltDatabase` is the same raw-dial family and a genuine cross-project vector, but it cannot use this guard — it runs precisely when `dolt_database` is unknown. It is already fronted by `resolveAuthoritativeServerMetadata`.

## Tests

`TestDestructiveFix_AbortsOnProjectIdentityMismatch` calls the real exported fixers and asserts a planted anomalous row **survives**, which is what proves the abort happens before any mutation. `TestDestructiveFix_SkipsOnUnverifiableTarget` proves the skip path returns nil and likewise leaves data untouched. `TestVerifyFixTargetIdentity` covers match, mismatch, and unverifiable-on-either-side, with each subtest building its own store so they are order-independent.

One honest limitation: the tests model the stale-port scenario by making the connection's stored `_project_id` disagree with local `metadata.json` — the observable effect of a fresh dial landing on the wrong project — rather than literally redirecting a port, since the package's tests share one Dolt container. That is called out in the test's doc comment.

```
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...            # clean
CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd/doctor/...  # clean
CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd/doctor/fix/... -count=1
ok  github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd/doctor/fix  16.248s
```

The broader `./cmd/bd/doctor/...` suite has pre-existing failures on this machine (`TestCheckRepoFingerprint_UsesTargetRepoOutsideCWD`, `TestCheckTestPollution_NoTestIssues_EmptyDB`, and intermittent dolt-connection-loss flakes) — confirmed identical on an unmodified baseline, unrelated to this change.

# Ready-work batch and the vishnujayvel wave-2 queue — 2026-07-28/29

Session shape: pick up `bd ready`, check every item against GitHub before starting,
batch and delegate. Four threads ran in parallel — three beads-source fixes in
isolated worktrees, and the upstream PR queue.

## Headline

- **The contributor waiting queue is drained.** `mybd-aayb` closed after verifying
  every entry PR-by-PR against GitHub rather than trusting the 07-25 snapshot.
- **PR #5101 is a data-loss fix, not output polish.** On `main`, the single-issue
  delete path gates the preview on `if !force` and the destructive branch below it
  never consults `dryRun`. So `bd delete <id> --force --dry-run` **actually deletes**.
  Approved and merged.
- **PR #5065 was stopped by a round-trip invariant that two independent model
  families found separately** — the strongest signal available that a finding is
  real rather than reviewer noise.
- **vishnujayvel replied on all 12 previously-reviewed PRs**, accepted our findings,
  and itemized exactly which changes they want pushed maintainer-side. That is
  now one batch: `mybd-php3l`.

## Upstream PRs handled

| PR | Author | Outcome |
|----|--------|---------|
| #5101 | idirectships | Approved, merged by patrol |
| #5099 | jacobhausler | Approved, merge lane armed |
| #5065 | halaprix | Comment review, two blockers, absorb offer open |
| #5129 | vishnujayvel | Re-review: approve with one should-fix |
| #5135 | vishnujayvel | Re-review: still needs changes, narrowly |
| #5142 | ours | Opened: doctor identity guard |
| #4329 | kevglynn | Cross-note on the #5065 collision |

### #5101 — forced dry-runs

The contributor's framing undersold it. `cmd/bd/delete.go:136` gates the preview on
`if !force`, and nothing below consults `dryRun`, so `--force --dry-run` deletes for
real. The PR's `if dryRun || !force` gate closes it. Verified the rest against code:
`force` only widens dependent discovery in `issueops/delete.go`, and the `dryRun`
return precedes every mutation on all four backends. One thing that looked like a
bug and was not: the error path calls `outputDeletionPreview` and then
`outputJSONError`, which would be two JSON documents — except the first writes to
stdout and the second to stderr.

### #5065 — the value of dual-vendor review

Two reviewers on different model families, run independently, returned the *same
two blockers*:

1. `StripGitHubSyncBlock` removes from the first start marker to the first end
   marker, while the renderer always appends its block at the end. An unpaired
   start marker — trivially produced by editing the visible `## Beads` section in
   GitHub's web editor, since HTML comments are invisible there — makes the next
   pull delete everything between. Measured, not hypothesized.
2. `ExtractBDIDFromGitHubSyncBlock` scans the *whole* body for `<!-- bd:` with no
   block, token, or prefix validation. A contributor copy-pasting a synced body into
   a new issue repoints an unrelated local bead and rewrites its `external_ref`.

Both are silent data loss. Posted as a comment review with an offer to implement the
fixes maintainer-side with authorship preserved (`mybd-fezwm`, deadline 2026-08-04).

## Beads-source work

Three fixes built in isolated worktrees, each independently reviewed before opening.
Both reviews came back **needs-changes**, and both sets of findings were real — worth
recording, because the temptation with builder output is to trust the green tests.

- **`mybd-2qegi`** — `doctor --fix` dials a fresh connection whose port resolution is
  independent of the store doctor diagnosed with, so a stale port file can aim DELETEs
  at another database. Now `#5142`. The review caught that `RecomputeBlocked` was left
  unguarded (bulk UPDATE plus a `DOLT_COMMIT` into another project's history, and it
  runs *last*, after every guarded fix has aborted) and that the guard was
  over-strict: hard-aborting on a missing project id would have permanently broken
  shared-server workspaces, which cannot self-heal because `CheckProjectIdentity`
  short-circuits when `.beads/dolt` is absent. Both fixed before opening.

- **`mybd-rr4x` Part A** — run the identity verifier when the target database already
  exists, even on the `CreateIfMissing=true` init path. Reviewer ran a negative
  control (reverted only the gate; the new test fails) confirming a genuine regression
  test. Found a remaining bypass: when `CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS` returns
  "database exists", that error *proves* pre-existence, but the code fell through
  with `dbExists` still false. Rework in flight.

- **`mybd-a4h6s`** — apply the `drainCall` pattern from merged #4504 to 16
  transaction-pinned `CALL DOLT_*` sites, where poisoning is worse because a pinned
  connection cannot be discarded by the pool. Review in flight.

All three are queued in the local verify queue rather than blocking a session on the
slow suite.

## Operational findings

- **`scripts/codex-agent scout` has no network.** Its read-only sandbox blocks
  `api.github.com`, so any `gh`-based recon fails after burning tokens — twice today,
  ~75k total. Codex is still the right tool for local source reading, which is where
  the cross-vendor value is. Fetch GitHub data to disk first, then point it at files.
  Recorded as memory `codex-scout-no-network`.
- **A bead's disposition can go stale under an active lane.** `mybd-k6zxf` still held
  a close-after-grace plan for #4376 while another session was refreshing that branch
  to land it. Annotated rather than executed. The check that caught it was reading
  GitHub before acting, not reading the bead.
- **The review-needed lane works.** It queued 20 PRs while this session ran, correctly
  distinguishing new arrivals from author replies and contributor pushes. The manual
  waiting-queue measurement that `mybd-aayb` was built around is now an audit tool,
  not the mechanism.

## Open threads

`mybd-php3l` is the big one: 12 PRs where the contributor has already told us exactly
which commits they want from us. Two are in progress (#5121, #5123). Also open:
`mybd-fezwm` (#5065 absorb, 08-04), `mybd-ma4ry` (#4329 / #5065 dedup collision),
`mybd-hk7hm` (legacy ADO `parent` row migration), and the follow-ups filed off the two
reviews: `mybd-h1vz1`, `mybd-jlgdx`, `mybd-2cxve`, `mybd-1s7pl`.

An independent reviewer checked all 16 converted sites and found the conversion itself correct and safe — no behaviour change at any site, error semantics preserved, no deadlock risk. The problem is the EXCLUSION set and the commit message. Apply the following in the same worktree, rebuild, re-run the targeted tests, and amend or add a commit with the same signed trailer.

REQUIRED:

1. Convert store.go:2533-2545 (concludeOpenMerge) and store.go:2605 (CommitWithConfig). Your stated rationale is factually wrong and an upstream reviewer will catch it. concludeOpenMerge does NOT run on a freshly acquired conn used once: it runs on the CALLER's pinned conn passed down from commitWorkingSet:2496, and the next thing that happens is commitWorkingSet returning into `defer conn.Close()` — which hands that conn BACK TO THE POOL via putConn. database/sql does not reset the driver conn, so an undrained buffer poisons the next borrower with ErrBusyBuffer. "Freshly acquired" is not a defence; being returned to the pool while busy IS the poisoning source. Both sites also swallow the error on the nothing-to-commit path, which is exactly the tolerate-and-continue shape the drain exists for.

2. Convert store.go:3396, :3404, :3409 (pullWithAutoResolve). This is the single most on-thesis site in the codebase and you excluded it. `_, pullErr := tx.ExecContext(ctx, query, args...)` for CALL DOLT_PULL tolerates its error and hands it to settleMergeInTx, whose own comment says it inspects conflicts "regardless of whether DOLT_PULL errored" — i.e. it keeps driving the same pinned tx after a tolerated CALL error. Line 3409 is worse: mergeErr is explicitly downgraded to nil on "up to date" and the tx continues. Converting 16 lower-risk sites while leaving this one invites "why did you stop here?".

3. Convert federation.go:446, :455, :456. `_, _ = conn.ExecContext(ctx, "CALL DOLT_BRANCH('-Df', ?)", ...)` discards an error that fires in the NORMAL case (no leftover staging branch), and the same pinned conn is reused immediately at :449. The :455/:456 pair sits in a defer that runs just before conn.Close() returns the conn to the pool. These were not in your left-alone list at all.

4. Fix the commit message. It lists only doltAddAndCommit's conn.ExecContext pair for store.go, but the diff also converts commitWorkingSet (:2502, :2517). It claims the converted operations include "create", but there is no CALL DOLT_ADD/DOLT_COMMIT pair in CreateIssue — creates route through doltAddAndCommit. And fix the concludeOpenMerge rationale per item 1.

5. Add a regression test. Nothing currently pins the tx sites to QueryContext, so a future edit reverts them silently. There is precedent on both sides: internal/storage/schema/lock_test.go:269-275 mocks CALL DOLT_ADD/DOLT_COMMIT as ExpectQuery precisely because they go through drainCall, and internal/storage/dolt/remote_routing_test.go:195 already uses sqlmock with a hand-built store and sqlmock.QueryMatcherEqual. doltAddAndCommit needs no schema, so `store := &DoltStore{db: db}` plus mock.ExpectQuery around a doltAddAndCommit call is roughly 25 lines and fails loudly ("call to ExecQuery was not expected") on any revert.

DECIDE AND REPORT, do not just skip: internal/storage/versioncontrolops/mergesettle.go (:72, :158, :209, :264, :339-340, :532, :548, :553, :569, :772, :868) is the largest remaining cluster of the same shape — TryAutoResolveMergeConflicts is reached from dolt/store.go:3722 with the merge tx, so the whole file runs CALL DOLT_* on a pinned tx with tolerated errors (:72 swallows "up to date", :340 is `_, _ =`). Its DBConn at versioncontrolops/db.go:15 is byte-identical to schema.DBConn, so schema.DrainCall drops straight in. Either convert it in this PR or state explicitly in the commit message that it is a known follow-up — silence is the one option that is not acceptable.

ALSO (nit, your call, say what you decided): the drainCall -> DrainCall forwarder is pure indirection over 14 in-package call sites; renaming drainCall to DrainCall and deleting the wrapper would be simpler. Separately, if you do convert mergesettle.go, note that three copies of the same DBConn interface then exist and a schema package is an odd home for a wire-protocol drain — worth a sentence in the PR body, not a refactor now.

Report back per numbered item, verbatim build/test lines, and the final commit SHA.
